desc: Normalize each pair to (a, b) with a < b, and group pairs by b (the larger endpoint).
For each b, compute the largest a (maxL[b]) and second-largest a (secondL[b]) among its pairs.
Compute base = sum over b of (b - maxL[b]), the number of valid subarrays with all pairs kept.
For each b, compute gain = maxL[b] - secondL[b] (secondL[b] = 0 if only one pair), representing extra subarrays freed by removing the pair achieving maxL[b].
Return base + max gain over all b; verify against both examples (9 and 12).
Confirm complexity O(n + m) time and O(n) space, fitting constraints n ≤ 1e5, m ≤ 2n.
Implement grouping per right endpoint: maintain max1, max2, cntMax for each b.
Compute bestGain = max over r of (max1[r]-max2[r] if cntMax[r]==1 else 0).
Test on examples and edge cases: no pair for many endpoints, duplicate pairs, all subarrays invalid except singles, m=1.
